content:
anya: Heads-up — the onboarding sample app hit a prefetch deadlock when token refresh fires during paginated prefetch. Repro is small and consistent.

anya: Steps: init cursor, prefetch window=3, auth token expires on background refresh, prefetch worker waits on lock and stalls new requests. Eventually app returns empty pages.

anya: Logs: 
```
prefetch: fetch(page=2) waiting for token refresh
auth: refresh started
prefetch: lock acquired? waiting
http: 401 -> queued retry
prefetch: starvation -> no further fetches
```

sam: Oof. Sounds like the refresh path grabs the same mutex the prefetcher needs? we saw similar in Go SDK but thought it was fixed.

jing: Can you paste the SDK + sampleapp settings? are you using the JS SDK or Go?

anya: JS SDK (v0.26.1) with sampleapp default prefetch. Config: `prefetchConcurrency: 3`, `retryOnAuthFailure: true`, `tokenRefreshSync: true` (we set sync for simplicity).

tyler: That `tokenRefreshSync: true` is the smoking gun. sync refresh blocks callers while it refreshes — if prefetch holds a slot and waits for auth, you can get a circular stall when all prefetch slots are blocked.

anya: Yep. Workaround was to set `tokenRefreshSync: false` and accept one failing request while refresh happens. But that feels brittle for onboarding docs.

sam: Long-term we should have non-blocking refresh + optimistic token swap in SDK: let prefetch continue with old short-lived token while refresh runs, and only replay failures. Also we should backoff prefetch attempts if many 401s in a window.

jing: Agreed. For parity: JS and Go SDKs need same behavior. Create a small patch: (1) refresh must not hold global prefetch lock; (2) prefetch should use a local token snapshot; (3) add `prefetchRetryWindowMs` to config.

tyler: Prototype patch I tried locally (JS):
```
// snapshot token before starting fetches
const snapshot = auth.getTokenSnapshot();
await fetchPage(page, { Authorization: `Bearer ${snapshot}` })
// kick off refresh in background, but don't block fetches
auth.refreshIfNeeded().catch(() => {/* handled by retry logic */})
```

tyler: Also added jitter to prefetch start times to avoid thundering-horse.

anya: Tested tyler's patch — no deadlock, pages flow, and UX is smooth. But we saw a slight increase in 401 retries (~0.5% -> 1.2%). Acceptable?

sam: Yes if we count that into telemetry and make it opt-in initially. Add metric `prefetch.auth_retries` and a flag `allowOptimisticPrefetch` default false for now.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy started for branch "prefetch-optimistic-2026" to dev cluster (deploy id: d-7982).

jing: Can you open a PR with unit tests that simulate token expiry mid-window? include a deterministic fake-clock test for jitter. ping me for review.

anya: Will do. I'll also update quickstart to recommend `tokenRefreshSync: false` for sampleapp until SDK parity lands.

sam: Nice. Once PR is in, mark an entry in changelog and add a short note to onboarding guide: "prefetch + short-lived tokens: enable optimistic prefetch or increase token TTL."

tyler: I'll riff on the Go SDK change and drop a mirror PR after your JS one lands.

anya: Thanks all :pray: saved a customer demo.
